title: Cement dust: a negative production externality, deadweight loss and the corrective tax
scenario: In an invented region, many perfectly competitive firms make cement. Dust from the plants dirties nearby homes and costs residents \$3 for every ton of cement produced. No one outside the market gains from it, and the plants do not pay for the damage.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the cement market showing demand, supply and marginal social cost. Show the socially efficient quantity, labeled QE.

slips.S: Supply shows only the plants' own costs; the efficient point uses MSC, which includes the dust.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled graph: Price and Quantity on the axes, D (= MPB = MSB), S (= MPC) and MSC above S
accept: P and Q on the axes
D, S or MPC, and MSC labeled, with MSC above S

rubric.point: QE shown where MSC crosses demand (MSB), at a smaller quantity than where S crosses demand

parts.sample: Price is on the vertical axis and Quantity on the horizontal axis. D = MPB = MSB slopes down; S = MPC slopes up; MSC lies above S by the \$3 external cost per ton. The market quantity QM is where D meets S. The efficient quantity QE, where D meets MSC, is to the left of QM and is marked with a dashed line to the quantity axis.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify whether the market quantity is greater than, less than or equal to the socially efficient quantity, and explain.

rubric.point: Greater than: firms produce where MPB = MPC and ignore the \$3 external cost, so they produce units whose MSC exceeds their MSB
accept: the market overproduces because private cost is below social cost

parts.sample: The market quantity is greater than the efficient quantity. The plants decide using their own marginal cost, MPC, which leaves out the \$3 of dust damage per ton, so the market produces where MPB = MPC. Between QE and QM each ton costs society more (MSC) than it is worth (MSB).

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Shade the area of deadweight loss that results from the market outcome.

rubric.point: The triangle between MSC and demand from QE to QM, fully shaded
accept: the area between MSC and MSB from the efficient to the market quantity

parts.sample: The deadweight loss is the triangle bounded by MSC above, demand below, and the vertical line at QM, with its point at QE where MSC meets demand.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Identify the per-unit tax on cement that would lead the market to the socially efficient quantity.

rubric.point: A tax of \$3 per ton, equal to the marginal external cost at the efficient quantity
accept: a tax equal to the external cost per unit

parts.sample: A tax of \$3 per ton, equal to the external cost per ton at the efficient quantity. It shifts supply up to MSC, so the market produces QE.
